I remember taking the wrong suitcase at baggage claim. I was beside the carousel, looking for my bag, and I saw one with a yellow strap like mine. I took it, thinking it was mine, but both bags had matching yellow straps. The other traveler was still waiting beside the carousel, and I’d picked up their suitcase.

That was the embarrassing part—realizing I’d been so sure just because of the strap. I hadn’t checked carefully enough. I keep track of stock at a bookstore, so I’m used to paying attention to which thing is which. It felt silly to get my own luggage wrong. I was mostly thinking about getting the bag back to the right person and wishing I’d looked more closely before taking it.
